subject: PO vs Card — Procurement & Payment Path for Redwood
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lopez <susan.lopez@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: PO vs Card — follow-up and next steps

Hi Susan — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery and next steps so procurement has everything they need: 

- Redwood pricing typically goes on subscription with an annual commitment.
- Two common payment paths we see: credit card for smaller pilot ARR (< $5k) and PO with Net30 for committed deployments and enterprise purchases.
- Many customers onboard as vendors (vendor packet + W-9) and optionally list Redwood in their marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) to enable marketplace billing.

Ask for you / procurement: can you confirm whether FintechCo requires vendor onboarding + PO for all new vendors above $5k ARR, or if a corporate card can be used for a pilot? Also, any preferred vendor form (we can fill your standard form) and who should we send the paperwork to?

I attached a short SOC2 summary and our vendor packet to help speed vendor onboarding.

Next steps I propose:
1) If PO required: I'll send a draft commercial summary + PO-ready invoice and our W-9/vendor packet.
2) If card is acceptable: we can enable a trial immediately and invoice via card.
3) Optional: we can get listed on your cloud marketplace — happy to connect you with our partnerships lead if you want that path.

Would love to align before looping legal/procurement. Are you available for a quick 20-min call Mon or Tue next week?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments:
- Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf
- Redwood_vendor_packet.zip

From: Susan Lopez <susan.lopez@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO vs Card — follow-up and next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the summary — helpful. Quick answers from procurement: 

- FintechCo requires vendor onboarding (vendor packet + W-9) for any vendor where expected spend > $5,000/year. For pilots under $5k, the finance team will accept corporate card.
- For anything that becomes multi-quarter / longer term we require a PO and Net30 terms (we can do Net45 in special cases).
- Procurement prefers our vendor packet to be filled out (I've CC'd procurement). We also use Workday for vendor creation; procurement will send a vendor onboarding link once they have the packet and W-9.

Can you send your standard commercial summary and a draft invoice for a PO amount (we'll use that to create the PO)? Also, please attach the completed vendor packet and W-9.

Best,
Susan Lopez
Head of Partnerships | FintechCo
Susan.Lopez@fintechco.com

Hi Susan — looping in our onboarding lead, Dev, to help with the vendor packet + Workday details. Marissa, attaching the vendor packet we generally fill and a completed W-9 (stub). Dev, can you confirm the typical timeline for vendor onboarding and what additional docs procurement usually asks for (SOC2, DPA, indemnity info)?

We typically see: 3-5 business days for packet review, and 7-10 business days for Workday vendor creation after procurement receives the packet. For PO/invoice generation — Marissa can provide a PO-ready invoice that procurement can use to create the PO.

Attaching: Redwood_vendor_packet.zip (contains standard form), W-9_MarissaCo.pdf, Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf

From: FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: PO vs Card — follow-up and next steps

Hi Marissa / Aditya,

Thanks for the packet. Procurement confirmed the following:

- Please send a draft invoice for the PO line item. We'll use that to issue a PO (Net30 standard).
- Once we have the vendor packet + W-9 uploaded into Workday, we will create the vendor record and link it to the PO.
- For marketplace billing: we prefer to transact directly where possible, but listing on the cloud marketplace is acceptable — it may add extra ops steps. If you can provide both a direct invoice and marketplace SKUs, we can evaluate which path is faster.

Procurement contact for follow-up: procurement@fintechco.com

Regards,
FintechCo Procurement Team

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks, everyone — quick summary and clear next steps so procurement can move: 

1) I'll send a PO-ready invoice (line items with SKUs + list price + start/end dates) to procurement@fintechco.com by end of day.
2) Aditya / Dev to provide completed vendor packet + W-9 (attached) — confirms we've done that.
3) Procurement to create Workday vendor and issue PO (Net30).
4) If procurement prefers marketplace billing, we'll also include marketplace SKUs in the invoice so you can choose the faster path.

Marissa here with a link to a 20-min slot tomorrow at 11am PT if anyone wants to jump on to finalize details: https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/20min

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this set up.

Best,
Marissa
